mechanisms.label: discrete height change
mechanisms.visibility_effect: visibility depends on the robot's height, not just its horizontal distance
mechanisms.physical_effect: climbing; horizontal progress alone is insufficient

mechanisms.label: elongated negative elevation
mechanisms.visibility_effect: the near lip occludes the target until the robot has descended and the far rim is cleared
mechanisms.physical_effect: the robot's own height changes along the route
mechanisms.note: solved by forward, forward - a genuinely multi-step case

mechanisms.label: localised negative elevation
mechanisms.visibility_effect: descending lowers the viewpoint and the far wall occludes the target
mechanisms.physical_effect: the viewpoint drops below the surrounding ground
mechanisms.note: solved by back, back - retreat is the correct action

mechanisms.label: lateral occlusion
mechanisms.visibility_effect: the target is behind a finite-width obstacle, so the sight line can be restored sideways
mechanisms.physical_effect: lateral bypass; moving closer does not help
mechanisms.note: the cleanest Closer is-not More-Observable case

mechanisms.label: periodic visibility transitions
mechanisms.real_world: dunes, wind ripples, rolling natural ground
mechanisms.visibility_effect: visibility flips repeatedly along the path (1 -> 0 -> 1 -> 0 -> 1)
mechanisms.typical_recovery: closed-loop re-observation; no permanently correct heading exists
mechanisms.note: the direct evidence that visibility is non-monotonic

mechanisms.label: broad concave elevation field
mechanisms.real_world: valleys, mining depressions, large settlement areas
mechanisms.visibility_effect: visibility varies continuously with elevation across a wide region, not at a single lip
mechanisms.physical_effect: the whole local viewpoint field shifts
mechanisms.note: must not be conflated with pit: local versus broad scale

mechanisms.label: spatially correlated natural relief
mechanisms.real_world: natural off-road ground, rock fields, unpaved roads
mechanisms.visibility_effect: occlusion is distributed over the local terrain rather than localised at one obstacle
mechanisms.physical_effect: continuous pose change along the route
mechanisms.note: procedural relief, not a claim of realism: Perlin noise is a representation of spatially correlated natural elevation

mechanisms.label: high-frequency natural relief
mechanisms.real_world: rubble, rock piles, debris fields, rough regolith
mechanisms.visibility_effect: irregular occlusion with no consistent geometry
mechanisms.note: the bridge from terrain to future-pose uncertainty
